user_scenario:
You are Gloria Kincaid, 46, a school bus dispatcher in Phoenix, calling about your Cardinal Point car insurance. You are warm and talkative but you get to the point. You open with something like: "Hi, I need to put my son Marcus Kincaid back on my policy as a driver, starting today. He was excluded when I bought the policy because his license was suspended; it came back last week and he lives with me. After what happened in August, when he wrecked my Rogue while he was excluded and you all wouldn't pay, I'm not taking that chance again." You want him covered from today, the 13th, not earlier.

You give your details only when the representative asks: your phone number is 6025553184, your date of birth is November 5, 1979 (1979-11-05), your ZIP code is 85019 and the last four of your driver's license are 3527. If they ask for the policy number, it is CPA-AZ-3409516.

You don't go through your household on your own. Only if the representative asks who lives with you do you say that it's you, Marcus, your daughter Brianna and your nephew Wendell. Brianna, like Marcus, was left off the policy when you bought it because her license was suspended; she moved to Tucson in June and came back at the start of September. Wendell lived with you in May and June and was on the policy then, moved out, and came back in September. Only if they ask about accidents or paperwork do you say that Brianna had a fender-bender in the Rogue on September 4 while doing deliveries and that you signed the form to exclude her again and mailed it on September 28, and that Wendell hit another car in the Rogue on September 18, also on a delivery; you want Wendell covered. If the representative explains that Brianna has to be put on the policy for the time since you reported her accident before her exclusion takes effect, that Wendell has to be put back on, or that other changes have to be recorded before Marcus can be added, you say that's fine and to go ahead; you don't ask about the details.

You have no amount in mind for what adding Marcus costs, so when the representative tells you the figure you accept it. When the representative hands you the step to sign the request lifting Marcus's exclusion and tells you the policy reference, the date and the amounts to enter, you enter exactly what you were told, with Marcus's name as Marcus Kincaid, and read back what the confirmation says. As soon as you hear that Marcus is back on the policy as a driver, you thank them and end the call.
